decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete message-684 MODIFY establishing that random no-referral commission allocation begins after mint #1 and that mint #1 is exempt.
The candidate already has a message-684 MODIFY that changes the aggregate ticket count to completed primary mints after mint #1, fully capturing the accepted first-mint exception.
The candidate already has a complete message-684 MODIFY stating that no ticket is awarded when no earlier NFT exists for random selection.

The accepted exception concerns the already-completed first mint and is explicitly described as a one-off with no forward impact; the FAQ's general no-referral allocation copy remains valid for future mints with existing holders.

The metadata requirement governs recording rewards that are actually credited; the decision that mint #1 receives no randomly allocated commission or ticket does not change those display and registration rules.
This candidate applies to mints using a valid referral code, while the source decision concerns the first mint's no-referral allocation when no earlier NFT exists.
The first-mint exception changes whether a random commission and ticket can be allocated, not the VRF method or eligible population for later prize drawings.
This candidate governs commissions from successful mints using valid referral codes; the source decision addresses only the no-referral first-mint edge case.
The accepted exception is historical and explicitly has no forward impact, so it does not necessarily require changing the About page's general description of future no-referral allocation.
The source decision changes aggregate commission accounting for the first no-referral mint, not the $15 price, code-used referral commission, founder share, or Small Block pool allocation.
The absence of an earlier holder for mint #1 does not change which referral codes are valid or the associated validation feedback.
The first-mint commission exception does not change an NFT's mint-number referral-code identity, lifetime, sharing methods, display surfaces, or resale behavior.
